full_judgment:
5. Mr Tufailur Rahman the learned Advocate appearing with Ms. Afreen Mohiuddin and Ms. Umme Salma on behalf of the appellants submits that the impugned judgment and decree is not sustainable in law in that the suit itself was barred by law of limitation under Article 86 of the Limitation Act. 

 7. Mr. Fazlul Haque the learned Advocate appearing with Mr. Akbor Hossain on the other hand, submits that the incident of fire took place in the suit premises on 21-2-97 at 12-30 hours out of electric short-circuit and the fire broke out at the godown premises of M/s Hamida Twisting Factory situated at Gosairbagh Panchasar and immediately thereafter Munshiganj Fire Service was informed about the incident at night and on the same day who having arrived at the scene tried their best to extinguish the fire and before the said fire came under control the entire stocks in the godown were completely burnt; a GD Entry with Munshiganj, Police Station was also lodged in connection with the same incident on 22-2-97 bearing No. 743 and that the mortgagee bank of the ensured property namely Agrani Bank, Mukterpur Branch notified the defendant Nos. 1-3 about the incident by their letter No.94-97 dated 22-2-97 and the plaintiff made formal claim with the Shadharan Bima Corporation for a loss of Taka 1,00,00,000 on 3-3-97 whereupon the defendant Nos. 1-3 appointed surveyors M/s GK Adjester Ltd, and M/s SS Surveyor Ltd. The said surveyors having conducted survey about the loss as claimed, by the plaintiff submitted their report recommending the claim of the plaintiff to the defendant Nos.1- 3, moreover there were other reports from different other agencies supporting the claim, of the plaintiff, despite such a position the defendants kept silence and ultimately on 30-5-2001 refused the claim of the plaintiff, therefore, the cause of action of the suit arose on 30-5-2001 and thereafter the instant suit was instituted on 8-10-2001, therefore, the learned Advocate for the respondents submits that the question of limitation as contemplated under clause (b) of, Article 86 of the Limitation Act does not arise at all. 

 11. The pertinent question about the applicability of clause (b) of Article 86 of the Limitation Act which prescribed a period of 3(three) years from the date of occurrence causing the loss. Before entering into the further discussion of the same we feel it proper to quote the relevant law which reads as under:— 

 13. In appreciating such submissions made by the learned Advocate we find that the entire gamut can be unfolded it the law as quoted above, is read together with first part of clause (b) of Article 86 of the Limitation Act which shows that the question a proof of the loss is very much pertinent in determining the loss itself and the quantum thereof and in doing so, the question of assessment, evaluation and verification about the claim ought to have been made as it has been done in the instant case by two surveyors as also by the police officer during investigation including the Fire Service men and upon accumulating all those reports the quantum of loss could be assessed which necessarily take sufficient time for the purpose, therefore, before assessment a claim for specific amount cannot be made by the plaintiff and that too has to be either accepted or refused by the insurer himself in the event of acceptance of the claim no question of filing the suit arise but only in the event of refusal of claim a institution of a suit necessitate. 

 14. In the instant case we find that the cause of action of the suit necessarily arose on the date of refusal of the claim of the plaintiff by defendant Nos. 1-3 on 30-5-2001 and the suit was instituted on 8-10-2001 and that before refusal of the claim of the plaintiff by the defendants a cause of action does not arise and a suit cannot be instituted, therefore, in our opinion, the law of limitation as quoted above, runs from the cause of action of a suit and that should be in all cases for 3(three) years not from the date of occurrence as noted by the learned Advocate for the appellants, therefore, we find that the instant suit has been filed well within the prescribed period of limitation as such in no way hit by clause (b) of Article 86 of the Limitation Act. Since all the questions raised by the learned Advocate for the appellants have already been answered, we do not find any other point raised by him, therefore, in our opinion the appeal itself is without substance.
